citation: [George M. Pullman residence, 1729 S. Prairie Avenue, completed.] Halftone of a photograph of the finished house from the south-west, across the crossing of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street; unknown photographer, undated (after the 1892 additions). Reproduced by the Glessner House Museum, 'Prairie Avenue in 1874' (blog, 2014-06-16).
author: unknown photographer
repository: Glessner House Museum blog (secondary reproduction; the original publication is not named). Prairie library image a16-ghm-blog-pullman-completed (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/images/stream-1600-1700.json).
locator: The foreground: the north-east corner of the crossing, where a cast-iron lamp post stands in a curbed grass plot at the curb corner, and, left of it on the Prairie Avenue parkway beside the walk, a post fire hydrant.
rights_note: A secondary web reproduction whose original source and rights are not stated (the Prairie library's ruling: 'unknown - link only'). Only what stands in the street and where is read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-27 (T-3199) from the image store's reference copy (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a16-ghm-blog-pullman-completed.jpg); the original host is not reachable from the build containers.
note: The same corner as the Detroit Publishing view (loc_det_4a08065_pullman_residence) from a little further west: the lamp in its curbed corner plot and the hydrant on the Prairie Avenue parkway north of it stand in both.
what_it_supplies: a gas lamp post at the north-east corner of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street, in a curbed grass plot at the curb corner
a post fire hydrant on the Prairie Avenue parkway beside the walk, north of that corner
